clue.text: Flush is something yet to be fixed at watering place?

indicators.note: one thing at another sits right next to it, so the second idea follows the first in the grid

blocks.note: a well is where water is drawn
a to-do is a task still waiting to be done

explanation.surface: A plumber notices a flushing problem at a spa that still needs repairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flush' looks like a toilet, but it is the adjective meaning having plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having plenty of cash, so a well-off person is described as well-to-do.

clue.text: Make better kipper

blocks.note: first meaning: to heal an illness
second meaning, a verb: to preserve fish by smoking or salting

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a smoked herring as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' reads as the smoked fish, but here it is the verb: to kipper a herring is to smoke it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure is both to heal a patient and to preserve meat or fish by smoking, which is what kippering does.

clue.text: Footwear, Sleepy's first pair with a lining

indicators.note: a first pair means only the opening two letters of the word are kept
a lining sits inside something, so these words are placed within the selected letters

blocks.note: the opening two letters of the dwarf's name
with means together with, and
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dwarf's shoes are described as a lined pair, in a puzzle themed on Snow White's companions.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle has a Snow White theme, so the dwarfs' names keep appearing; here Sleepy just supplies its opening two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe held on with straps, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Foyer out of bounds in place of worship with no time for worker

indicators.note: outside the boundary means the edge letters of the word are lost
in means placed inside the other word
having none of something means that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a temple is a building for worship
T is the standard abbreviation for time
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is barred from the entrance hall of a church and has no time for a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foyer out of bounds' sounds like a no-entry sign, but it means the word loses its edges; 'worker' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An employee is someone who works for an employer, a worker on the payroll.

clue.text: Character on staff to make 200% more departed shortly

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: adding 200% to something makes it three times as big
the setter intended split apart; the published wording does not really mean this

explanation.surface: A musical instruction to make the sound three times louder, with the conductor leaving early.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter admitted an editing slip: the original read 'parting shortly', parting = CLEFT. 'Departed' can only give LEF(T), which leaves the C unexplained.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble clef is the sign written on a musical stave to fix the pitch of the notes, a character on the staff.

clue.text: Tense dons run after Snow White

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so one word wraps round the letter like a garment

blocks.note: to chase is to run after
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Nervous academics pursue Snow White.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers, but it is the verb to put on; 'Snow White' is the definition, not just the theme heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure as the driven snow and white as innocence: chaste means sexually pure and virtuous.

clue.text: Grumpy reversing Aussie pickup into factory

indicators.note: something reversing goes backwards, so the vehicle's name is read from the end
going into means being placed inside the other word

blocks.note: ute is the Australian name for a utility pickup truck
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered driver backs an Australian truck into a factory; Grumpy is also one of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant means childishly sulky and bad-tempered, a synonym of grumpy.

clue.text: Was don tense when speaking?

indicators.note: when speaking means the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: taut means tense or stretched tight

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a university lecturer was nervous while giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, so 'was don' means acted as one: taught. 'Tense' here is the adjective, not grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university lecturer, so to have been a don, teaching students, is to have taught.

clue.text: Soggy sheep knocked over Bashful

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so the animal's name is read backwards

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
shy is a synonym of bashful

explanation.surface: A shy dwarf, Bashful, gets bowled over by a sheep in a wet field.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy land is waterlogged like a marsh, so soggy underfoot.

clue.text: College sportsman panted audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to blow is to puff and pant

explanation.surface: A university athlete is out of breath after a race.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a Blue is a student who has represented the university in a sport against the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blue is an Oxbridge sportsman awarded colours for competing against the rival university.

clue.text: Musician has large drink before the fish

definitions.note: the answer is strictly the instrument, used for its player

indicators.note: before places the first item ahead of the second in the answer

blocks.note: a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits
bass is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A musician has a big drink before the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: In an orchestra players are often named after their instrument, so the double bass can be the person who plays it.

clue.text: Gland making many sick finally removed

indicators.note: the final part removed means the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: tons means a great many
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A swollen gland that made many people sick has finally been taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: The tonsils are two masses of lymphoid tissue at the back of the throat, often called glands.

clue.text: The outline's reproduced, not new

indicators.note: something reproduced is made again, here with its letters in a new order
not means without, so that letter is struck out of the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written, reading the apostrophe-s as an S
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An outline drawing has been copied, so it is no longer new.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read plainly it describes a silhouette, an outline copied as a shadow, and the same words supply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is the dark shape or outline of something seen against a light background.

clue.text: Coward's work causing Sneezy to summon Doc?

definitions.note: a description of the condition rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a 1925 comedy by Noël Coward
second meaning, the affliction that would make the sneezing dwarf call the doctor dwarf

explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward was an English playwright; 'Coward's work' tempts a solver towards something cowardly. Sneezy and Doc are two of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy to pollen makes sufferers sneeze, so it would send a sneezer to a doctor, and it is also the title of Coward's play.

clue.text: Pudding is hot, Dopey!

blocks.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit purée and cream
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone calls Dopey the dwarf out for complaining that the dessert is hot.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of stewed fruit folded into cream or custard.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means stupid or slow-witted, which is what foolish also means.

clue.text: Doc was raised on fillets

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means turned upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top
in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: taken as written before being turned round
to fillet a fish is to bone it, so fillets as a verb means bones

explanation.surface: A doctor was brought up eating fish fillets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fillets' reads as a noun on a plate, but it is the verb for taking bones out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is old slang for a surgeon or doctor, from the amputations of earlier medicine.

clue.text: Monstrous seashell is helical to some extent

indicators.note: only to some extent means just a part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A grotesque seashell has a partly spiral shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellish describes something dreadful or atrocious, as monstrous does.

clue.text: Bashful member of flock is last in church

indicators.note: last in means only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: a sheep is one animal of a flock
taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A shy member of a congregation sits at the back of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flock' suggests a church congregation, but here it really is sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish means awkwardly shy or embarrassed, close to bashful, also the name of one dwarf.

clue.text: Left one in short dress, merrymaking

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word
short means cut off at the end, so the word drops its last letter

blocks.note: a frock is a dress
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone left one person wearing a short dress at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short dress' looks like a mini skirt, but 'short' cuts FROCK to FROC before L and I go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is a bout of lively play or fun, the same thing as merrymaking.

clue.text: RAF woman redesigned naval ship

indicators.note: something redesigned is put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An air force woman has redrawn the plans for a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-of-war is an armed sailing ship of a navy, a historic warship.

clue.text: Rising artist skilled and potentially productive

indicators.note: in a down entry something rising goes upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
able means skilled

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming artist is talented and may well be prolific.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is fit for ploughing and crops, so it could produce a harvest.

clue.text: One bringing court case about very loud bear

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: someone who sues in court
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A plaintiff goes to court over a noisy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear pain or hardship is to endure it, which is to suffer it.

clue.text: Pinch shellfish, cold not hot

indicators.note: one thing not another means the first letter takes the place of the second

blocks.note: a shrimp is a small crustacean
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, the letter replaced

explanation.surface: Someone steals seafood served cold rather than hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' looks like steal, but here it means to economise.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch and scrape is to be frugal, and to scrimp is likewise to save by spending as little as possible.

clue.text: Cricketer finally wore hard hat after cap disintegrated

indicators.note: finally means only the word's last letter is kept
something disintegrated has fallen to pieces, so its letters are scattered and rebuilt
after places the hat word behind the other piece in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word
a bowler is a stiff, round felt hat

explanation.surface: A cricketer ended up in a hard hat because his cap fell apart.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a pace bowler delivers the ball fast rather than with spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pace bowler is a fast bowler, a specialist type of cricketer.

clue.text: Transported under cover, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: wrapped means covered up

explanation.surface: Goods were shipped secretly, according to a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' looks like shipped, but it means carried away with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be enraptured, completely absorbed or delighted, which is what rapt means.

clue.text: Announcer's made out a list of duties

indicators.note: an announcer speaks the words, so they are taken by sound

blocks.note: to make out a cheque or list is to write it

explanation.surface: A broadcaster has drawn up a staff schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule saying who does which job and when, a list of duties.

clue.text: Happy and Dopey dropping ring

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: blithering means utterly foolish, as in blithering idiot
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Two dwarfs, Happy and Dopey, are bell-ringers who give up ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy and Dopey' read as two dwarfs side by side, but only Happy is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree, which is a synonym of happy.

clue.text: Sleepy comes to with a shaking

indicators.note: being given a shaking jumbles things up, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The dwarf Sleepy regains consciousness after a good shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes to' reads as waking up, the opposite of the answer, which makes the surface neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Comatose means in a deep stupor, or jokingly very drowsy, a stronger sense of sleepy.
